blogs.title: From Web Crawls to Math Mastery: How DeepSeekMath Harvested 120 B Tokens of Math Data
blogs.description: A behind‑the‑scenes look at the data‑collection pipeline that turned the public Common Crawl into the DeepSeekMath Corpus. We'll explain the fastText classifier, iterative domain expansion, de‑duplication, multilingual filtering, and why this web‑scale approach outperforms arXiv‑heavy corpora.

blogs.title: Why Starting from a Code Model Boosts Mathematical Reasoning
blogs.description: An accessible walkthrough of the experiments showing that pre‑training on code before math (or mixing code with math) dramatically improves both step‑by‑step and program‑aided problem solving. The post breaks down two‑stage vs. one‑stage training, the role of catastrophic forgetting, and what this means for future LLM design.

blogs.title: Teaching LLMs to Think Like Mathematicians: Chain‑of‑Thought, Program‑of‑Thought, and Tool‑Integrated Reasoning
blogs.description: Explains the three instruction‑tuning paradigms used in DeepSeekMath‑Instruct—plain CoT, PoT (writing Python), and tool‑integrated reasoning. Readers will see sample prompts, why each style matters, and how they together lift performance on benchmarks like GSM8K and MATH.

blogs.title: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): A Memory‑Efficient Twist on PPO for Math RL
blogs.description: Demystifies the new GRPO algorithm by comparing it to classic PPO, showing how it replaces the critic with group‐average baselines, cuts memory use, and still yields big gains on GSM8K and MATH. Includes visual analogies and a simple step‑by‑step example of the GRPO update.

blogs.title: Putting It All Together: How DeepSeekMath 7B Reaches 51.7% on the Competition‑Level MATH Benchmark
blogs.description: A narrative summary of the full training recipe—base model init, 500 B token math pre‑training, instruction tuning with CoT/POT/TORA data, then GRPO RL—and how each stage contributed to the final score. Highlights open‑source vs. closed models and what “self‑consistency over 64 samples” means for users.
